stories.title: Nvidia’s next CEO: The outside contenders to succeed Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Rene Haas, Lisa Su and Tim Cook are among the names floated as Nvidia faces a defining choice between technical leadership and seasoned management.

sources.title: Nvidia’s next CEO: The outside contenders to succeed Jensen Huang
sources.text: The biggest guessing game in business has begun: Who can fill Jensen Huang’s shoes? Colette Kress, chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013, was appointed interim CEO of the company on Thursday. Kress will also continue in her CFO role as the board conducts its search for Jensen Huang’s permanent successor. “Colette is very much the right interim CEO,” Scott W. Simmons, co-managing partner of executive search firm Crist Kolder Associates, told Fortune . But Simmons, who has worked in executive recruiting for almost 30 years, thinks Nvidia’s board will seek a technologist as Huang’s permanent successor, potentially from outside the company. If Nvidia goes with an external candidate for the CEO job, Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at The Futurum Group, is putting his money on Arm CEO Rene Haas. “He spent seven years at Nvidia and understands Jensen’s culture; and what makes him interesting is that Nvidia’s Grace and Vera CPUs run on Arm architecture,” Boloor wrote in an X post . “So while he missed [the] rise of NVLink, Mellanox and rack-scale AI he understands [the] CPU side of Nvidia’s platform better than almost anyone else on the outside.” Sam Sugarman, a venture capital and private equity investor who co-founded and leads the VC/PE Secondaries practice at Concordia Capital, also placed Haas on his list of external candidates . Haas would bring a combination of Nvidia experience and public-company leadership, having steered Arm through its 2023 IPO and expanded its business beyond processor licensing. His background spans engineering, product strategy and sales. But his familiarity with Nvidia dates to an earlier era: he left in 2013. The board will have to assess whether running Arm has prepared him for Nvidia’s much larger, more complex business. Sugarman also pointed to AMD CEO Lisa Su as a potential successor to Huang. Su (who ironically happens to be a distant cousin of Huang’s) would bring a combination of semiconductor engineering credentials and a proven record of running a major chipmaker. She has led AMD since 2014, overseeing a turnaround that made it a formidable competitor in processors and a challenger to Nvidia in AI chips. That experience could appeal to a board. But recruiting her would mean persuading a sitting CEO to leave the company she rebuilt. Meanwhile, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., told Fortune that he sees Tim Cook , the former CEO of Apple ; Tom Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud; and Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks , “as the top three external candidates for Nvidia’s CEO role.” Cook would bring experience with a challenge few executives have faced: succeeding a technology company’s defining leader. Cook took over from Steve Jobs and spent 15 years running Apple before becoming executive chairman in September. Cook’s mastery of supply chains and logistics would be a good fit at Nvidia, and the fact that Apple has developed its own processors in-house over the past decade means Cook has some direct experience in the chips business. His continuing work on Apple’s international relationships would also be relevant to a company navigating geopolitical pressures. But his continuing responsibilities at Apple as chairman could complicate the prospect of recruiting him. That said, Cook has the support of one high-profile observer: President Trump posted on Truth Social Thursday that Cook should replace Huang. Kurian would offer a connection to Nvidia’s AI infrastructure business. Before taking over Google Cloud in 2019, Kurian spent 22 years at Oracle , ultimately becoming president of product development. At Google Cloud, he has also worked closely with Nvidia through the companies’ AI infrastructure partnership. The question is how readily that experience would translate to leading the chipmaker itself. Arora would bring the experience of a sitting public-company chief executive with a career spanning enterprise technology, global sales and investment. Before joining the cybersecurity company in 2018, Arora was president and COO of SoftBank and held senior commercial roles at Google, including chief business officer. His appeal as a candidate could depend on whether Nvidia wants a strategist who can build around its technical leaders. There may be pros and cons for each potential candidate, but the board’s choice will ultimately determine Nvidia’s fate. “There’s such a small pool to fish in when you think about people capable of stepping into this,” Simmons said.

sources.title: NVIDIA podría destituir a Jensen Huang como CEO tras el escándalo con la espía china
sources.text: Jensen Huang podría perder su puesto como director ejecutivo de NVIDIA . De acuerdo con The Wall Street Journal , la junta directiva estaría preparando una reunión para decidir el futuro del fundador y CEO de la compañía. Las cosas se complicaron para Huang luego de que una investigación interna descubriera vínculos con una supuesta espía china. Según el reporte, el consejo de administración considera destituir a Huang después de que salieran a la luz dos relaciones extramaritales . Hace unos días, el CEO reconoció que había sido infiel a su esposa y pidió disculpas por traicionar la confianza de su familia y de la organización. La figura en el centro de esa polémica es Alice Huang, una ejecutiva de la compañía Megaspeed y con vínculos con el gobierno de Xi Jinping. Los primeros rumores apuntaban a que Megaspeed habría ayudado a desviar chips de IA hacia China . La compañía, con sede en Singapur, se convirtió en uno de los principales clientes de NVIDIA para la construcción de centros de datos de IA en el sudeste asiático. No obstante, las autoridades estadounidenses sospecharon que Huang ayudó a contrabandear tarjetas gráficas , por lo cual abrieron una investigación a finales de 2024. La relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang comenzó en 2023 y permitió que la ejecutiva china desviara 240.000 placas gráficas H100, H200 y A100 hacia el gigante asiático. The Information reveló que Huang montó una red de empresas en China junto con su hermana y esposo, incluyendo una que le ayudó a convertirse en socio preferente de NVIDIA. Este movimiento le garantizó acceso prioritario a los chips y al CEO de la empresa. Hace unas semanas surgió un reporte de que Alice Huang estaba vinculada a los servicios de inteligencia chinos. El Departamento de Justicia abrió múltiples investigaciones relacionadas con ella y el mundo se le vino encima al jefe de NVIDIA. Según informó el New York Times , Alice Huang (también conocida como Huang Le) trabajaba para el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China mientras mantenía una relación romántica con el directivo de la empresa de tarjetas gráficas. Los investigadores temen que pueda haber accedido a detalles técnicos sobre el hardware de IA de NVIDIA y las discusiones internas con la Casa Blanca. Hasta ahora, las autoridades se han centrado en su papel como ejecutiva de Megaspeed, donde aprovechó su cercanía con Jensen Huang para ayudar a eludir los controles de exportación estadounidenses. Además de esta relación, el New York Times señaló que el jefe de NVIDIA mantuvo un romance con otra empleada de la compañía . Kimberly Powell, vicepresidente del área de atención médica de NVIDIA, fue captada en un vídeo con Jensen Huang mientras se encontraban en un hotel de San José, California. Las políticas internas de la compañía prohíben este tipo de acciones, sobre todo cuando se trata de una relación extramarital entre un jefe y su subordinada. Hasta el momento de esta publicación, el futuro de Jensen Huang permanece en el aire . Si la junta decide apartarlo del cargo, NVIDIA perdería al hombre que transformó la compañía y la convirtió en una de las más valiosas del mundo. Huang ha sido el rostro visible de la empresa por más de tres décadas, primero en su etapa gamer y ahora en el desarrollo de chips para centros de datos, por lo que encontrar un sucesor será un trabajo complejo.

sources.title: Jensen Huang renuncia ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia após admitir traição
sources.text: Por Gabriel Cavalheiro | 12/11/2026 às 11:48 • Atualizado 12/11/2026 às 11:56 O CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, renunciou ao cargo nesta quinta-feira (12) , após admitir publicamente uma relação extraconjugal com a ex-diretora da Megaspeed International e empresária Alice Huang. A executiva é investigada por espionagem a serviço do Ministério de Segurança do Estado da China. A atual CFO da empresa, Colette Kress, foi nomeada CEO interina enquanto o conselho busca por um novo executivo para assumir o cargo. A renúncia de Huang acontece após 33 anos na liderança da Nvidia, que tem vivido um dos seus melhores momentos por liderar o boom da inteligência artificial e fornecer componentes para data centers de IA. No ano passado, a empresa foi a primeira do mundo a ultrapassar os valores de mercado de US$ 4 trilhões e US$ 5 trilhões. A relação extraconjugal entre o ex-CEO da Nvidia e Alice Huang levantou preocupações sobre a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos e o mercado de chips de IA . No último domingo (8), o ex-chefão da companhia de chips admitiu a traição em meio a um escândalo de espionagem chinesa . "Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações a machucaram, assim como aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz. Sinto muito", escreveu o então CEO. O jornal The New York Times relatou que Jensen Huang estaria envolvido em um segundo caso , desta vez com a vice-presidente de health care da Nvidia e subordinada direta do ex-CEO, Kimberly Powell , segundo cinco funcionários da companhia. As políticas internas da Nvidia orientam os funcionários a “evitar situações em que nossas ações criem conflito”, incluindo “relacionamentos pessoais”. O acúmulo de escândalos envolvendo o ex-presidente fez com que as ações da empresa caíssem 8% nesta quarta-feira (11). A companhia também perdeu US$ 1 trilhão de valor de mercado . Em comunicado enviado à imprensa, o conselho da Nvidia agradeceu as contribuições de Jensen. "A Nvidia é uma das empresas de tecnologia mais impactantes do mundo. O conselho e a empresa agradecem a Jensen por suas contribuições imensuráveis para a companhia e para a indústria", diz a mensagem. A companhia está iniciando uma busca por um Chief Executive Officer permanente e considerará candidatos internos e externos . Até lá, Kress ocupará o cargo de CEO de forma interina. “A força da Nvidia sempre veio de suas pessoas e, junto com nossa equipe de liderança, estou comprometida em construir sobre a base extraordinária que Jensen criou ao longo dos últimos 33 anos”, destacou a executiva. O empresa também anunciou que Harvey C. Jones assumirá a posição de primeiro presidente do conselho. Na próxima terça-feira (17), a Nvidia divulgará seus resultados financeiros referentes ao terceiro trimestre do ano fiscal de 2027. Vale lembrar que, em setembro, a companhia adquiriu a Hugging Face, o que levantou a dúvida se a plataforma continuará com código aberto após a compra.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal
sources.text: Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors today announced the resignation of Jensen Huang, now former chief executive and president of the artificial intelligence chipmaker, amid a scandal, naming Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. The news arrives following numerous industry reports that the board intended to replace Huang as CEO after revelations of a second extramarital relationship with an executive at Nvidia, coming mere days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. News initially broke over the weekend that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang , no relation, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and an alleged Chinese spy. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang facilitated $7.5 billion in chip sales to China. According to another report, Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who serves as vice president of healthcare. The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities concluded Alice Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset. Upon revelations of the affair, the Associated Press reported that President Trump announced that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the allegations, while adding, “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” Late Wednesday, the Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust Huang and discussed a potential replacement as CEO. Huang has no obvious single successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. Reportedly, the board sought counsel from an outside firm to find someone to fill the role. With the announcement, Nvidia stock was falling more than 5% in trading today, backing off an even steeper loss at the opening. Yahoo Finance calculated that Nvidia has lost more than $600 billion in market value since the previous Thursday, likely with more shocks to come. “Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.” Kress has served as executive vice president and CFO since joining in September 2013. Her accolades include leading the company’s finance organization and working to build the company’s dominance in the AI chip industry. Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The CFO was intimately involved with Nvidia’s widespread financing of AI compute providers, in particular its backing of not only AI leaders OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC — the latter set to go public as early as next week — but also neoclouds such as CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV. Those financings have been criticized by some as “circular,” meaning Nvidia essentially invested in customers so they could use the money to buy more of its graphics processing units. The potential successors to Huang, who had 30 direct reports, include no one obvious choice and a succession plan apparently was not in place. Candidates that some have speculated about include Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia years ago, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing and creator of its CUDA software considered the real moat for its business. “The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Forrester Vice President and Group Research Director Stephanie Balaouras told SiliconANGLE in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.”” Balaouras added that “tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers and investment plans.” Huang is best known for co-founding Nvidia in 1993 in a San Jose Denny’s and has served as its CEO since. His departure will likely send further ripples through the AI silicon and software industry. He has been deeply involved in Nvidia’s product strategy and built longstanding customer relationships, helming the company as it became the behemoth it is today. Nvidia commands roughly 80% of the data-center AI chip market, although industry estimates vary by methodology. Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. puts its share of AI computing power shipped at 63% in the second quarter of 2026. Other market carve-outs include custom chips built by cloud companies within the broader supply, including Google LLC’s tensor processing units at 25%, Amazon Inc.’s custom silicon at 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI hardware accelerators at 4%. sources.title: Nvidia busca CEO tras la salida de Jensen Huang: estos son los candidatos que suenan para el puesto
sources.text: Nvidia ha perdido al único director ejecutivo que ha tenido jamás. Jensen Huang ha dimitido este jueves como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración, y la empresa ahora tiene que encontrar a alguien para dirigir al fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo. Por el momento, el puesto pertenece a alguien de la casa. Qué ha pasado. Nvidia anunciaba que su directora financiera, Colette Kress, actuará como directora ejecutiva interina mientras mantiene su cargo financiero, y que el consejo buscará candidatos internos y externos para el puesto permanente. También ha nombrado a Harvey C. Jones, antiguo director ejecutivo de Synopsys, como presidente del consejo, siendo de hecho el primero en la historia de la empresa. La salida de Huang se produce tras las investigaciones sobre sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, una de ellas presuntamente con Alice Huang , ejecutiva y directora de la empresa Megaspeed, sospechosa de ser espía china . Las acciones de Nvidia abrieron este jueves con una caída de más del 13 % tras la dimisión, borrando más de medio billón de dólares en valor. La nueva CEO interina : Colette Kress. Ha sido directora financiera desde 2013, trabajó anteriormente en Cisco y Microsoft, y aparece junto a Huang en cada presentación de resultados. Josh Gilbert, analista de eToro, declaraba a Reuters que es “la opción obvia para mantener el rumbo” y una voz de confianza para los inversores. Ahora, que se quede de forma permanente es otra cosa. Para Gilbert la ventaja de Nvidia es la tecnología y el consejo probablemente querría a un ingeniero al mando. Los ingenieros. Ian Buck, quien ayudó a desarrollar CUDA, el software que mantiene a los desarrolladores vinculados a los chips de Nvidia, y que ahora dirige los productos de IA a hiperescala, encabeza la lista para llevarse el puesto permanente. Shay Boloor, estratega jefe de mercado en Futurum Equities, contaba a Reuters que es el candidato interno más fuerte por ese motivo. Otros miembros internos mencionados incluyen al cofundador Chris Malachowsky, el único ejecutivo al nivel de antigüedad de Huang, y a Andrew Bell, vicepresidente sénior de ingeniería de hardware, con una trayectoria destacada en el sector de los chips. Los externos. Si el consejo mira más allá de Nvidia, que es algo que también plantean según el comunicado, el nombre que más suena es el del director ejecutivo de Arm, Rene Haas, antiguo ejecutivo de Nvidia. Tiene “sentido lógico”, según comparten en Reuters, pero tal y como comparte Charu Chanana, estratega de inversiones del banco Saxo, el modelo de negocio de Arm difiere considerablemente del de Nvidia. ¿Y la familia? . Los dos hijos de Huang ocupan cargos ejecutivos en Nvidia, aunque todavía son relativamente jóvenes e “inexpertos”, según relatan desde la BBC. Armina Rosenberg, de Minotaur Capital, ve plausible también una estructura de codirección ejecutiva, combinando a un líder financiero como Kress con un líder tecnológico como Buck. Qué pasa ahora. De momento, y hasta conocer más noticias, tendremos que esperar al próximo martes 17 de noviembre, que es cuando Nvidia presenta sus resultados del tercer trimestre bajo el mando de Kress. sources.title: Trump pide a Tim Cook como CEO de NVIDIA tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang: «Una leyenda por otra leyenda»
sources.text: La renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA es, sin dudas, el tema del día . El escándalo por infidelidades le ha costado al empresario el puesto que ostentó durante los últimos 33 años , y el asunto promete seguir dando que hablar por bastante tiempo. Lo más curioso es que todos tienen una opinión sobre el tema y hasta Donald Trump ha propuesto a un reemplazante de alto perfil: Tim Cook . En las horas posteriores a la salida de Jensen Huang, Trump usó su perfil en Truth Social para postular a Cook como próximo CEO de NVIDIA. De acuerdo con el presidente de Estados Unidos, el exCEO de Apple es la única persona que tiene lo necesario para hacerse cargo de un rol tan complejo. A sabiendas de cómo piensa y actúa Donald Trump, no quedan dudas de que el mandatario estadounidense habla en serio. Claro que hoy parece improbable que Tim Cook esté dispuesto a asumir un rol tan notorio fuera de Apple, en especial por lo repentino y desastroso del desenlace de Jensen Huang. "Ahora que el CEO de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, quien ha hecho un trabajo fantástico, ha renunciado, solo hay un hombre capaz de tomar su lugar: Tim Cook, de Apple. ¡Una leyenda reemplaza a otra leyenda! Presidente Donald J. Trump", publicó el presidente de Estados Unidos. Más allá de las virtudes de Jensen Huang y Tim Cook para conducir durante gran cantidad de años (y con gran éxito) a sus respectivas empresas, Trump no ofrece detalles de por qué el exjefe de Apple debería reemplazar a su antiguo colega en NVIDIA. Tal vez solo sea porque Cook ha sabido congraciarse con el presidente estadounidense durante sus mandatos, tal y como lo hizo Huang en su momento. Sea como sea, todavía no se sabe quién reemplazará definitivamente a Jensen Huang. Colette Kress , la jefa de finanzas de NVIDIA, fungirá de CEO interina hasta que se designe a un nuevo responsable del cargo. La junta del gigante verde anunció la puesta en marcha de un proceso de búsqueda de nuevo consejero delegado, para la cual analizará a candidatos internos y externos. Asimismo, se ha designado a Harvey C. Jones como presidente del board , el primero en ocupar ese rol en la historia de la compañía. ¿Tiene posibilidades Tim Cook de ser el próximo CEO de NVIDIA? Hasta hace menos de 15 días, era inaudito pensar en dicha empresa sin Jensen Huang como jefe, pero ya hemos visto que los imposibles no existen y que no se puede descartar nada. Dicho esto, Cook se encuentra extremadamente cómodo en su nuevo rol como presidente ejecutivo de Apple. Además, no es un directivo enfocado en producto como sí lo fue Jensen Huang ; algo que podría no importar en cualquier otra empresa, pero que ha sido crucial para el crecimiento de NVIDIA bajo el comando de un único CEO en sus 33 años de vida. Ya veremos qué novedades surgen en tal sentido.

sources.title: Ex-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is set to testify before Congress this month
sources.text: House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast said the hearing will take place before Thanksgiving. Jensen Huang might have stepped down from his roles at the top of NVIDIA, but he won't be sliding out of the spotlight just yet. The company's former CEO and president is set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, according to House representatives. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said Huang agreed to testify on Wednesday — hours before NVIDIA announced his resignation with immediate effect — after lawmakers threatened him with a subpoena. It appears the hearing will take place behind closed doors (which is unfortunate, because that's likely to be some spicy testimony). However, Mast expects it to be filmed and transcribed, according to Bloomberg . The House's Intelligence and China-focused committees will join the Foreign Affairs cohort for the hearing. "Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but NVIDIA is a very important company to the United States of America," Mast said. "I don't want to see anything hurt in NVIDIA, but he has some very serious questions to answer." NVIDIA has been in turmoil after it emerged over the weekend that the company was investigating Huang over an affair to which he admitted, allegedly with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating the situation as well. On Wednesday, it was reported that Huang had another affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. The company's board met later that day to determine Huang's future. Colette Kress, NVIDIA's executive vice president and chief financial officer, is stepping in as interim CEO while the company seeks a permanent successor. Meanwhile, the Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Alice Huang , the alleged spy, to determine whether entities associated with her were involved in attempts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China. The DoJ is also said to be taking the lead in an investigation into her former company, the Singapore-based Megaspeed International, over alleged smuggling of US-made chips into China in defiance of export restrictions. The company said it would cooperate with the probe . Officials in Singapore opened an investigation into Alice Huang, Megaspeed and associated individuals last year. The Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement on Thursday that she was barred from re-entering the country after police determined she knowingly offered up inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed. However, they "concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated." The investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is ongoing.

sources.title: Elon Musk says it would be an 'honor' to hire Nvidia's Jensen Huang
sources.text: SpaceX founder and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said it would be "an honor" to hire embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , after reports emerged that Nvidia's board could be preparing to oust Huang from the company. Late Wednesday stateside, financial blog Zerohedge wrote on X, "Elon please hire Jensen," to which Musk replied , "That would be an honor." The post comes as the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to discuss Huang's future at the company. The report also followed a New York Times story that Huang had an extramarital relationship with another Nvidia executive. The developments sent Nvidia shares down more than 8% in after-hours trading. Huang and Nvidia have dominated headlines since the weekend after the Nvidia CEO acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a business executive whom U.S. intelligence identified as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang, also known by her Chinese name Huang Le, was recruited to gather information on Jensen, according to people briefed on the intelligence cited by The New York Times. The Nvidia chief sought to project a "business as usual" atmosphere on his first day back at the office after the revelations, but he is now facing calls to resign from several lawmakers. Sen. Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., a member of the Senate Banking Committee, reiterated Wednesday his call for Huang to resign, joining Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee and Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC.

sources.title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia. Elon Musk says hiring him would be ‘an honor’
sources.text: Before Nvidia publicly announced Jensen Huang’s departure, Elon Musk said he wanted to hire him. “That would be an honor,” Musk wrote on X Wednesday evening, responding to a post that read: “Elon please hire Jensen.” The exchange followed a Wall Street Journal report that Nvidia’s board was preparing to oust its cofounder, according to Reuters . By Thursday morning, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, CEO, and a director, effective immediately. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, and longtime director Harvey Jones becomes Nvidia’s first board chair. The exit removes the cofounder who built Nvidia into the chipmaker at the center of the AI boom and No. 16 on the 2026 Fortune 500. Investors had already felt it: Nvidia lost $450 billion in market value in the days after Huang admitted to an affair, Fortune reported. That affair was with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia cloud partner . U.S. intelligence officials reportedly believe she was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence, which Beijing denies. Huang publicly apologized for his infidelity on Sunday. Nvidia’s board initially stood by him, saying on Sunday , “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team,” even as it announced an independent investigation. It said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security had been compromised. But on Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang had also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reported directly to him. The board reportedly met later that day to decide his future. After the resignation was announced Thursday, Reuters reported that Huang had also had an intimate relationship with another Nvidia employee, citing two people familiar with the matter. Nvidia and Huang have not confirmed the report. Musk’s five-word response did not specify a job, a company, or whether the two had discussed working together. But it suggested that losing the job Huang held for 33 years had not entirely spoiled his employment prospects. In September 2024 , Oracle cofounder Larry Ellison recounted a dinner with Musk and Huang at Nobu in Palo Alto, where he and Musk found themselves pleading for more of Nvidia’s coveted graphics processing units. “I would describe the dinner as Oracle—me and Elon begging Jensen for GPUs,” Ellison said. “Please take our money. Please take our money. By the way, I got dinner. No, no, take more of it. We need you to take more of our money please.” Musk has since made his admiration public on several occasions. “I am a huge admirer of Nvidia and Jensen btw. That market cap is well-deserved,” he wrote on X in March , adding that SpaceX AI and Tesla expected to keep buying Nvidia chips at scale. The relationship extends beyond business. In May, a user posted photographs of the pair taken a decade apart with the caption: “The most important thing in life is having true friends.” Musk reposted it with one word : “True.” In October, he struck a more personal note on X : “Old friends are the best friends. Jensen rocks.” The post accompanied a clip of Huang discussing the companies’ collaboration on computing infrastructure for space. The admiration goes both ways. Huang said Musk was “working on exactly the right things,” Fortune reported in January 2025 , and later that year called Musk “the ultimate GPU,” comparing his ability to juggle complex information to the chips Nvidia sells. Musk is far from the only prominent business figure who thinks Huang still has something to offer. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney urged Nvidia’s board to retain him on X , comparing a potential dismissal to “ Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy.” He credited Huang with driving successive eras of technology, from gaming graphics to AI supercomputers. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman took a more personal approach , arguing that even exceptional people make mistakes and urging support for Huang and his family. Sequoia Capital partner Shaun Maguire criticized Huang’s conduct but described him as “irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.” Musk endorsed Maguire’s post with a brief reply: “I agree.” Others who publicly backed Huang include Anduril founder Palmer Luckey , Binance founder Changpeng Zhao , and 37signals CTO David Heinemeier Hansson . The support offers a glimpse of the network Huang could draw on for whatever comes next. For now, that next chapter remains unannounced. Musk’s public welcome has not come with a job description, and it is unclear whether Huang intends to join another company, start something new, or step away from running one. His departure also does not resolve Nvidia’s internal investigation or the FBI inquiry into his relationship with Alice Huang , which President Donald Trump has said is underway. Financially, Huang has plenty of room to weigh his options. He still holds about 3.6% of Nvidia, making him its fourth-largest shareholder, according to Reuters . His net worth fell roughly $10 billion this week to about $145 billion, Fortune reported , knocking him out of the world’s 10 richest people. A divorce could cut that net worth substantially. His wife, Lori Huang, could be entitled to half, depending on any marital agreements and which assets qualify as separate property, Forbes reported . Neither has publicly announced plans to divorce. Before any new role, Huang has a date on Capitol Hill. He has agreed to testify before lawmakers, with an appearance expected before Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said, according to Bloomberg . Mast has said Huang has “very serious questions to answer.”

sources.title: NVIDIA prepara demissão de Jensen Huang após segundo caso de traição
sources.text: Por Raphael Giannotti | 12/11/2026 às 11:34 Se você é PC gamer, viu Jensen Huang, fundador e único CEO da história da NVIDIA, subir ao palco e apresentar novas placas de vídeo por anos. Isso pode mudar daqui pra frente, já que o conselho administrativo da empresa está discutindo a demissão do executivo agora após outro caso extraconjugal vir à tona . Segundo o The Wall Street Journal, a diretoria se prepara para destituir o líder que comanda a gigante dos semicondutores há 33 anos, em uma reunião decisiva que pode selar a primeira troca de comando desde a fundação da companhia em 1993. O estopim para a mudança drástica foi uma reportagem do The New York Times revelando que Huang manteve um relacionamento com Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente da divisão de saúde da própria NVIDIA e sua subordinada direta . O caso se soma ao escândalo recente envolvendo a empresária e executiva Alice Huang , suspeita de atuar como agente da inteligência chinesa. Essa crise de governança e segurança nacional já fez as ações da fabricante despencarem 20% na bolsa de valores desde o início das revelações. De acordo com relatos de funcionários citados pela imprensa norte-americana, Huang e Powell foram vistos trocando carinhos em um hotel em San Jose, na Califórnia, durante a conferência GTC em março . Embora o código de conduta da NVIDIA não proíba expressamente todos os relacionamentos entre gestores e subordinados, as normas internas exigem que potenciais conflitos de interesse sejam reportados ao departamento jurídico. Além disso, trata-se de uma quebra de aliança matrimonial. Para conduzir a apuração independente, o conselho contratou o escritório de advocacia Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Caso a demissão de Huang se confirme, a empresa enfrentará um vácuo inédito de liderança: como o executivo mantém uma estrutura administrativa horizontal onde dezenas de vice-presidentes respondem diretamente a ele, não há um sucessor natural óbvio. Enquanto isso, os trabalhos dentro da gigante seguem, já que os data centers não podem parar. Para os gamers, tem sobrado cada vez menos. Parceiras da NVIDIA já até afirmaram que a empresa tem interrompido o fornecimento de chips para a fabricação de placas de vídeo GeForce RTX .

sources.text: O Conselho de Administração da Nvidia anunciou nesta quinta-feira (12) que Jensen Huang renunciou aos cargos de presidente, diretor-executivo e membro do conselho da empresa. A decisão tem efeito imediato. O fundador da Nvidia admitiu ter sido infiel à esposa após a revelação de um relacionamento com Alice Huang, suspeita de espionar para o governo da China. Apesar do sobrenome em comum, ela não tem parentesco com Jensen Huang. As ações da Nvidia desabaram mais de 24% em 30 dias. A empresa perdeu US$ 1,081 trilhão (cerca de R$ 6,1 trilhões) em valor de mercado entre 29 de outubro e 10 de novembro, segundo levantamento da Elos Ayta. No domingo (8), a companhia abriu uma investigação independente para apurar se ele foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência de outro país. Nesta quarta (11), o jornal New York Times revelou que Jensen também teve outro caso extraconjugal, desta vez com Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente da área de saúde da Nvidia. Em comunicado, a Nvidia informou que Colette Kress, atual vice-presidente executiva e diretora financeira, assumirá temporariamente o comando da empresa. Segundo a empresa, Kress teve um papel fundamental no crescimento da Nvidia à frente da área financeira. Antes de ingressar na companhia, ela acumulou quase 25 anos de experiência em cargos financeiros em empresas de tecnologia, incluindo Cisco e Microsoft. Comunicado da Nvidia sobre afastamento de Jensen Huang “O Conselho de Administração da NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) anunciou hoje que Jensen Huang renunciou aos cargos de Presidente, Diretor Executivo e membro do Conselho, com efeito imediato. Colette Kress, atual Vice-Presidente Executiva e Diretora Financeira da NVIDIA, concordou em atuar como Diretora Executiva Interina. Kress continuará atuando como Vice-Presidente Executivo e Diretor Financeiro enquanto atua como Diretor Executivo Interino até que um sucessor permanente seja nomeado. O Conselho está iniciando uma busca por um Diretor Executivo permanente e considerará candidatos internos e externos. Kress atua como Vice-Presidente Executivo e Diretor Financeiro da NVIDIA desde que ingressou na empresa em setembro de 2013. Durante seu mandato, ela liderou a organização financeira da empresa e desempenhou um papel fundamental no crescimento e evolução da NVIDIA. Antes de ingressar na NVIDIA, Kress passou quase 25 anos em cargos financeiros em empresas líderes de tecnologia, incluindo Cisco e Microsoft. O Conselho de Administração nomeou Harvey C. Jones como seu primeiro Presidente do Conselho. O Sr. Jones é empreendedor, executivo de tecnologia e investidor ativo de capital de risco há mais de 30 anos, incluindo atuando como Diretor Executivo e Presidente Executivo da Synopsys. “Colette ajudou a conduzir a NVIDIA durante um período de crescimento extraordinário e possui profundo entendimento do nosso negócio, clientes, operações e posição financeira”, disse Harvey Jones, presidente do Conselho de Administração da NVIDIA. “Ela conta com o apoio de uma equipe de liderança experiente que tem sido fundamental na execução da estratégia da NVIDIA e no avanço de seu roteiro tecnológico. O Conselho tem total confiança em Colette e na equipe de liderança, e esperamos que as operações da empresa, compromissos com clientes e roteiro de produto continuem sem interrupções.” “A força da NVIDIA sempre veio de suas equipes e, junto com nossa equipe de liderança, estou comprometido em construir sobre a extraordinária base que Jensen criou nos últimos 33 anos”, disse Colette Kress, CEO interina e CFO da NVIDIA. “Continuaremos avançando no trabalho que tornou a NVIDIA líder em computação acelerada e IA, e executaremos as oportunidades que virão. Nosso foco permanece em servir nossos clientes, parceiros, desenvolvedores e acionistas.” As contribuições de Jensen para a NVIDIA são profundas. A NVIDIA é uma das empresas de tecnologia mais influentes do mundo. O Conselho e a empresa agradecem a Jensen por suas contribuições imensuráveis para a empresa e para a indústria. A NVIDIA divulgará seus resultados financeiros do terceiro trimestre fiscal de 2027 na terça-feira, 17 de novembro, por volta das 13h20 PT, conforme previsto anteriormente, seguido pela teleconferência de resultados às 14h PT.”

sources.title: Saída de Jensen Huang abala Nvidia e pode redefinir o futuro da inteligência
sources.text: A renúncia de Jensen Huang ao comando da Nvidia abre uma incerteza que vai além da sucessão na fabricante de chips: a continuidade das relações comerciais e financeiras que ajudam a sustentar a expansão da inteligência artificial. O executivo tinha papel central na articulação de investimentos entre empresas do setor. A mudança ocorre em um momento em que fabricantes de semicondutores , provedores de nuvem e desenvolvedores de IA dependem de grandes compromissos financeiros para ampliar a infraestrutura necessária ao treinamento e à operação de modelos. A influência da Nvidia no mercado não se limita à venda de processadores. A empresa também participa de um ecossistema de investimentos e acordos com companhias que precisam de capacidade computacional para desenvolver serviços de inteligência artificial . Nesse arranjo, provedores de nuvem e laboratórios de IA dependem de infraestrutura equipada com chips da fabricante, enquanto os investimentos e compromissos comerciais ajudam a viabilizar novas instalações. Huang teve participação direta na construção dessas relações. Sua atuação envolvia não apenas a estratégia tecnológica da Nvidia, mas também a articulação com parceiros e clientes que impulsionam a demanda por seus produtos. A saída do executivo, portanto, levanta dúvidas sobre a capacidade da companhia de manter esse ritmo de coordenação. O desafio não está necessariamente no desenvolvimento dos próximos chips . A Nvidia conta com equipes técnicas e um planejamento de produtos que não dependem exclusivamente de seu fundador. A questão é como a empresa manterá a rede de acordos, investimentos e operações que conecta diferentes participantes do mercado de IA. Um dos pontos de atenção é o chamado financiamento circular. O modelo ocorre quando empresas que fornecem tecnologia ou infraestrutura também investem em clientes ou oferecem garantias que ajudam a financiar compras de seus próprios produtos e serviços. Esse tipo de relação pode acelerar a construção de data centers e a expansão da capacidade computacional. Ao mesmo tempo, cria vínculos financeiros entre empresas que dependem umas das outras para manter seus planos de crescimento. Se compromissos forem revistos ou novos investimentos demorarem a sair, os efeitos podem alcançar diferentes partes da cadeia. Anúncios e acordos envolvendo empresas como OpenAI , CoreWeave e Anthropic ilustram a dimensão dos recursos mobilizados para ampliar a infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. A continuidade desses projetos depende de financiamento, disponibilidade de equipamentos e confiança na demanda futura. A renúncia de Huang não significa que esses compromissos serão interrompidos. Mas sua saída acrescenta uma variável à avaliação dos investidores: quem assumirá a articulação de negócios em um setor no qual decisões de investimento de uma empresa podem influenciar os planos de várias outras? A reação inicial das ações mostrou a dimensão da preocupação dos investidores. Os papéis da Nvidia recuaram mais de 12% nas negociações iniciais desta quinta-feira (12), movimento que poderia retirar cerca de US$ 500 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 2,78 trilhões) de seu valor de mercado. AMD e Broadcom, por outro lado, registraram altas de 2% e 5%, respectivamente. A diretora financeira Colette Kress assumirá o comando interinamente, enquanto a empresa avalia candidatos internos e externos para a sucessão definitiva. A Nvidia também terá de demonstrar que consegue preservar sua estratégia comercial e os relacionamentos construídos por Huang. O desempenho financeiro recente oferece uma base operacional robusta: a companhia reportou US$ 96,2 bilhões (cerca de R$ 533,9 bilhões) em receita no último trimestre. Ainda assim, os próximos resultados, previstos para 17 de novembro, serão acompanhados não apenas pelos números de vendas, mas também por sinais sobre demanda, entregas e novos investimentos. O alcance da transição será medido, portanto, pela capacidade da Nvidia de manter sua posição na cadeia de infraestrutura da IA. Mais do que encontrar um novo CEO, a empresa precisa mostrar que o ecossistema de negócios construído durante a gestão de Huang pode continuar funcionando sem depender de sua presença direta. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.title: A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? O que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang
sources.text: O dia 12 de novembro de 2026 ficará marcado no mundo da tecnologia como um dos mais improváveis e até mesmo mais importantes de sua história. Nesta quinta-feira, Jensen Huang, o CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, renunciou ao cargo após um escândalo de adultério e espionagem. As reações do mercado de tecnologia e Wall Street já eram esperadas. Somente nas últimas horas, as ações da companhia verde caíram mais de 13%. O próprio Huang saiu do seleto grupo das dez pessoas mais ricas do mundo nos últimos três dias ao perder quase US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 50 bilhões) de sua fortuna absurda, estimada em mais de R$ 700 bilhões. Por mais que a indústria de tecnologia e o segmento de IA possam enfrentar um período de incertezas, a expectativa é que esse mercado continue firme. No entanto, a pergunta que uma generosa parcela do público começa a fazer é: o que acontece com os gamers de computador? Além do gigantismo em IA, a Nvidia é dona da tradicional linha de placas de vídeo GeForce, que alimenta 72% dos computadores dos gamers, segundo dados da Steam. Jogar no PC e usar uma Nvidia GeForce se tornou basicamente um sinônimo para muitos, e agora impera o medo de que essa divisão esteja ameaçada. A Nvidia publicou uma nota recente que explica a renúncia de Jensen Huang como diretor da empresa. Interinamente, Colette Kress atuará como CEO da companhia até que a empresa e o Conselho encontrem um executivo (a) definitivo. Em outras palavras, as portas da Nvidia estão abertas e não há como prever integralmente quais mudanças serão implementadas na gigante. Mesmo assim, a curto e até médio prazo talvez seja seguro dizer que a divisão GeForce de placas de vídeo ficará intocada. É verdade que a Nvidia já direcionava seus esforços quase que totalmente para o segmento corporativo, mas isso não quer dizer que a empresa abandonará seu braço de gráficos e GPUs. Arthur Igreja, especialista em tecnologia e inovação, aponta que o estágio embrionário do momento impossibilita fazer previsões assertivas . No entanto, ele explica que é improvável a Nvidia simplesmente se livrar da linha gamer, afinal de contas, ninguém parece disposto a se livrar de uma divisão inteira assim. Uma coisa é ter foco, outra, completamente diferente, é abrir mão. Essa ainda é uma linha de receita importante para a Nvidia. O especialista salienta que em momentos de crise, como o atual, a companhia precisará reunir todas as suas linhas para maximizar o lucro. O fato de a divisão GeForce existir pode até mesmo ser um fator positivo para a companhia. Aliás, a nova CEO era diretora financeira da empresa, então ela deve saber da importância dessa série e pode evitar cortes desnecessários agora. Claro, isso não significa que os produtos GeForce ficarão intocados para sempre . Um futuro CEO pode entender que a linha gamer e de itens domésticos não faz sentido e focar toda a infraestrutura da empresa para o setor corporativo. Mesmo assim, isso seria um movimento brusco extremamente arriscado. Vale notar que o mundo do hardware doméstico contempla apenas três empresas: Nvidia, AMD e Intel. A AMD é a única com força para produzir amplamente CPUs e GPUs, e a Intel engatinha no cenário das placas de vídeo. Abrir mão da série GeForce seria entregar o mercado de bandeja para a AMD e ver a Intel ganhar terreno ao longo dos anos. Arthur Igreja também aponta que o movimento de saída de Jensen Huang da Nvidia também não deve ser motivo para reduzir a crise de componentes global. “A questão da demanda é um fator externo, exógeno. Ela depende muito mais das hyperscalers e do restante do mercado, além de fatores como um eventual aumento da regulação [...] Em última instância, a NVIDIA continua sendo uma fornecedora. Ela não representa o mercado como um todo e não controla a demanda”. Mesmo com sua atuação distante do segmento gamer, Colette Kress já mostrou em algumas oportunidades que entende o fenômeno. Durante uma conversa com analistas da JPMorgan na CES 2026, a executiva foi questionada sobre a ausência de novidades para o setor na feira e respondeu que “o negócio de games tem sido um sucesso estrondoso”. Aliás, a própria entrada de Kress na Nvidia em 2013 aconteceu por conta do setor de games. Ela entrou na companhia após seus filhos recomendarem a marca por conta dos bons produtos gamer que produzia. O TecMundo já possui um ótimo conteúdo que conta detalhadamente a história completa da Nvidia, mas é sempre bom relembrar como um gigante se ergue. Tudo começou em 1993, quando Curtis Priem, Christopher Malachowski e um jovem chamado Jensen Huang fundaram a Nvidia em Sunnyvale, na Califórnia. Engana-se quem pensa que a estrada até o sucesso da Nvidia foi pavimentada com ouro - ou melhor, silício. O primeiro chip comercial da companhia surgiu apenas em 1995, o NV1, mas foi em 1997 que as coisas realmente começaram a engrenar graças ao sucesso da linha Riva. Mas foi em outubro de 1999 que a linha GeForce deu seu passo inaugural com a GeForce 256. Jensen e seus amigos acreditavam que os computadores se tornaram uma plataforma multimídia e de jogos 3D. A chegada da GeForce 256 confirmou isso ao se tornar a primeira GPU como conhecemos hoje. De 1999 até 2026 tem muita história para contar. A Nvidia comprou rivais, como a 3dfx, desenvolveu o chip do primeiro Xbox, do PlayStation 3, fez com que os usuários pudessem usar várias placas de vídeo em um único PC e por aí vai. Lá em 2008 a companhia verde resolveu lançar uma placa chamada GTX 280. A partir de então, as GTX se tornaram as placas de vídeo definitivas para os jogadores, mesmo a rival AMD tendo adquirido a fabricante de GPUs ATI para rivalizar forças. Não tinha jeito, a Nvidia dominava esse segmento. Os anos passaram e uma década depois da introdução da GTX 280 a Nvidia resolveu revolucionar o mundo dos PCs de novo: entrou em cena a linha RTX. Esses produtos, que perduram até hoje, tinham o poder para calcular raios de luz em tempo real, o Ray Tracing, e isso possibilitou que os games ficassem exponencialmente

Markets were on tenterhooks ahead of the decision amid reports that the chip giant's board had convened to discuss his future with the company. The New York Times on Wednesday reported that Huang had engaged in a second extramarital affair with an employee. The CEO was already under scrutiny after Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy. Nvidia announced on Thursday morning that, following a board meeting, Huang would step down after more than 30 years at the company's helm. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Those downgrading the stock included longtime Nvidia bull Ben Reitzes of Melius Research. Nvidia shares were seen down more than 12% shortly after the open on Wall Street, bringing losses for the last month close to 25%. Here's what analysts and investors are saying about the company and the stock. Reitzes changed his rating for Nvidia to hold from buy. His price target is now $185 — down from $315 — is 6% above the level at which shares last closed. "We thought we had experience, but nothing prepares you for what has happened at Nvidia over the last few weeks - and especially since Saturday. The only situation remotely close to this we can recall was HP in 2010. Waiting to see what that Board would do (and who they would hire) that time didn't work out. It was really cheap, too, at ~9x EPS right after its initial swoon. Nvidia is a much stronger, more important company, but its market moves far faster, and this story touches geopolitical flashpoints. sources.title: AI industry execs brace for future without leading hype man, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
sources.text: Tech industry insiders awoke Thursday morning with an unfamiliar, and somewhat alarming notion to contemplate: life without Jensen Huang. Huang’s abrupt resignation as CEO leaves one of the world’s most valuable companies without the leader who has steered it for the past 33 years; the person who almost singlehandedly transformed Nvidia from a small maker of video game graphics chips into the driving force of the AI boom. “NVIDIA’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom,” Stephanie Balaouras, Forrester’s VP, group research director, told Fortune . The importance of Nvidia, and of Huang, to the AI industry extends well beyond the company’s own P&L statement. In addition to being the leading maker of the GPU chips powering AI services like ChatGPT and Claude, Nvidia has become the AI industry’s “central bank” financing scores of other companies. And then there’s Huang’s unique standing as AI’s senior statesman and cheerleader on everything from AI regulation to industrial policy. Whether the AI industry turns out to have lost its most famous champion with the ignominious exit of Huang and his famous black leather coat, or a more crucial, Jenga-like piece may be the most important economic question to be answered in the coming weeks and months. “Obviously Nvidia is more than Jensen Huang, but he kind of championed a whole range of investments,” a VC investor focused on early-stage companies told Fortune . “There is a question around whether the pace of investment in AI and the size of the amounts of capital going into companies can be continued. Because by any stretch of the imagination, it’s been quite extreme,” the investor said. In the immediate aftermath of the news, the stock market appears to be keeping its composure. While shares of Nvidia were down 6.3% in midday trading on Thursday, and certain AI-linked stocks took a hit, the broader market reaction was relatively muted, with the Nasdaq down only 95 points. But with spending on AI and data centers so important to the broader U.S. economy, the extent of the potential fallout from the Nvidia shakeup is difficult to overstate. Looming largest on the horizon is Anthropic’s widely anticipated initial public offering , scheduled to occur next week. The Anthropic IPO (along with OpenAI’s IPO expected in 2027) represent make-or-break moments for the AI industry—closely watched events that will serve as proxies for the health, and momentum, of the AI business. If nothing else, one startup founder told Fortune , the Nvidia drama raises the stakes for Anthropic’s upcoming IPO: “If the Anthropic IPO doesn’t go well and if the OpenAI IPO [down the line] doesn’t go well, there’s a question of: Is there a path to profitability for any players in the AI space?” Antropic is seeking to raise upwards of $60 billion in the offering slated for November 18, giving the five-year old AI company a valuation that could exceed $1.4 trillion when it makes its expected Wall Street debut next week. Karl Alomar, a partner at venture firm M13, argued that investors will recognize the strength in Anthropic’s business, regardless of the Nvidia shakeup. “From where I stand, Anthropic is still in as good, as strong and as good a position as it was before this news came out,” Alomar said. “I’m not sure it’ll have a massive impact on them. Anthropic’s numbers are fantastic, and they’ve clearly shown that they have excess capacity for what they need,” he said. Anthropic’s business prospects are closely intertwined with those of the cloud providers, which provide the data centers and compute capacity to train and run AI models like Claude. (According to Anthropic’s S-1 filing, it has roughly $900 billion in compute spending commitments over the next several decades.) While the tech giants like Alphabet , Amazon , and Microsoft have the wherewithal to ride out whatever turbulence is caused by the changes at Nvidia, the situation may be trickier for the smaller “neo-cloud” companies —many financed by Nvidia—that buy Nvidia chips in bulk and rent out the computing power. Huang has championed these neo-cloud companies because it was good for business and the company’s influence, Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners and one of the few on Wall Street with a sell rating on Nvidia’s stock. “He’d rather have 300 small customers who are dependent on him than three massive ones who you can’t negotiate with,” he said. With Nvidia CFO Coleen Kress now serving as interim CEO, the company’s attitude towards neo-clouds could shift. According to a report in The Information on Thursday, Kress has occasionally pushed back against Huang’s deals in the AI ecosystem, including a deal to backstop $250 billion in credit for an OpenAI datacenter project. The “Nvidia money train” that has kept parts of the market that propped up could come to an end, said one venture capital partner invested in numerous AI startups. “ The idea that they could count on Nvidia for future financing is unlikely.” Shares of CoreWeave one of the leading neocloud providers were down 7.5% on Thursday, while Nebius Group, another neo-cloud company which gave a lighter-than-expected sales forecast during its quarterly earnings on Thursday, were down 18%. Investors are likely to look harder at the numbers Huang used to justify the complex web of investments. Jason Schloetzer, an associate professor at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business, expects investors and policymakers alike may start re-examining “Jensen math.” U.S. policy towards data centers could also come in for harsher treatment, particularly after last week’s midterm elections in which voters overwhelmingly registered their opposition to having the facilities built in their communities. sources.title: ‘That Nvidia guarantee is not worth what it was worth a week ago’: What Jensen Huang’s exit means for neoclouds
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia hits the AI industry’s most indebted borrowers hardest, according to one investor who backs AI infrastructure. Nvidia said Thursday that Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. His exit follows his admission of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe to be a Chinese spy, and following a board investigation into the affair. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO , and the board named Harvey Jones its first chair. While Nvidia’s leadership switch-up is sending shockwaves across every industry that relies on its chips to those who simply have stock or their 401Ks resting in company, some say the companies that are most at risk are the so-called neoclouds that rely on Nvidia’s chips. Nvidia designs the chips that most AI models are trained on, and Taiwan’s TSMC manufactures them, and that’s a problem. So says Joe Kaiser, who started Switchyard Partners at the beginning of this year after serving as CEO of Mercato Partners, which managed about $1.5 billion. Neoclouds such as CoreWeave and Nebius buy those chips by the hundreds of thousands, fill data centers with them and rent the computing power to AI labs and other companies, competing with Amazon , Google and Microsoft . But Nvidia does more than sell to them. It invests in them: the company held about $329 million in Nebius shares, for example, at the end of June. Nvidia also guarantees their business. In July, Nvidia began offering to rent back unused GPU capacity from neocloud partners at a fixed rate, a floor meant to make banks more willing to lend. The company later joined a $500 billion financing platform with six institutional partners, of which Nvidia may backstop up to $125 billion. That backstop, Kaiser said, posed an issue for what lenders are pricing. “The chip isn’t what puts them at risk, but it’s the financial backstop that allows CoreWeave or Nebius to go get those hundreds of millions of dollars of debt from Blackstone and Brookfield ,” Kaiser told Fortune . “Why is Blackstone willing to back a CoreWeave project? It’s because they know that there’s an Nvidia backstop, a written backstop, behind it, and so it lowers the risk, and then obviously lowers the interest rate.” CoreWeave carried $35 billion in debt at the end of June, and lenders had grown wary of businesses that depend wholly on AI demand, well before Huang left. “If the capital providers now say that Nvidia guarantee is not worth what it was worth a week ago, that puts those neocloud businesses at risk,” Kaiser said. “At the end of the day, this is a heavy-asset, infrastructure-based industry.” OpenAI and SoftBank’s SB Energy may be the biggest beneficiaries of Nvidia’s backstops, with CoreWeave and Nebius close behind. Kaiser referenced how Nvidia has been in talks over a reported $250 billion backstop to help OpenAI lease an Ohio data center campus that SB Energy is developing. Following Huang’s resignation, Neocloud stocks fell Thursday: CoreWeave dropped about 9%, giving back part of a 25% rally the day before. Nebius fell 16% , though it also issued weak full-year guidance the same day. Nvidia itself lost about $450 billion in market value in the days after Huang admitted the affair, before Thursday’s drop. Kaiser doesn’t expect Nvidia to lose its grip on AI training for at least two or three years, because customers built on its CUDA software will find it “really hard” to switch. The fight is over inference, the work of running models once they’re trained, which Kaiser said now takes up more AI compute than training. There, buyers are weighing Nvidia’s general-purpose chips against cheaper ones built for specific jobs: Qualcomm for robotics, Cerebras, Etched, Google’s TPUs and Amazon’s Trainium. “If Nvidia no longer has Jensen as its rainmaker, did that just tip the scale towards using specialized chips?” Kaiser said. “The bigger play is actually for the specialty chip makers,” he said, but said AMD and Broadcom will inevitably gain an opening. Google and Amazon could win twice: by pitching their own chips to labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, and by lending their balance sheets. “The Googles and others can step into that Nvidia backstop arrangement,” he said. TSMC should come through fine, Kaiser said. He estimated about two-thirds of its capacity goes to Nvidia, but said it could shift that to other customers “in pretty short order.” Kaiser said Huang ran Nvidia on a “hub-and-spoke” model. “The stories are true about Jensen having 60-plus direct reports,” he said, which now leaves “this leadership vacuum and vision vacuum.” He referenced Intel after Andy Grove stepped down as CEO in 1998. “Andy Grove and Jensen both have just this iron-fist approach to management, very disciplined approach,” he said. Intel kept growing revenue after Grove left, he said, but the company lost margin and “didn’t adapt as well” as chip demand moved toward new uses. “Intel is the roadmap here to what might be ahead for Nvidia.” Kaiser also tied Huang’s exit to last week’s midterms, where data centers became a campaign issue. Calling Huang the industry’s “true spokesperson” for data centers, and with that spokesperson now gone, he said, the case for giant single-site data centers weakens further. “This is just more push for distributed edge compute,” he said, “away from these mega monolithic data centers.”

sources.text: Nvidia's leadership shake-up is unlikely to cause immediate disruption for major Asian semiconductor suppliers, such as Samsung Electronics and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., but Jensen Huang's departure has raised questions about the company's longer-term product strategy and supply chain relationships. The bigger issue for investors and suppliers is whether Nvidia can maintain the pace of innovation and close ties with key partners that Huang helped drive as the company built its dominance in artificial intelligence chips. In a Friday research note, Nam Dae-jong and Kim Yeon-mi, analysts at South Korean brokerage Daol Investment & Securities, said Huang's departure was unlikely to affect the semiconductor industry's near-term outlook. However, they flagged uncertainty over Nvidia's medium- to long-term product roadmap, including how its new leadership would coordinate with partners across the AI ecosystem. For chipmakers in Asia, one key question is whether Nvidia's relationships with its manufacturing partners could change under new leadership. Nam and Kim expect Nvidia's foundry relationship with TSMC to remain unchanged, given the companies' established partnership. They also expect Nvidia's relationship with Samsung's foundry business to continue, citing growing cooperation between the companies, including manufacturing involving Samsung's 4-nanometer process and work on next-generation high-bandwidth memory technology. The analysts said custom AI chips, or application-specific integrated circuits, or ASICs, are emerging as alternatives to Nvidia's graphic processing units and could accelerate diversification in the AI chip market. However, they cautioned against interpreting growing competition as a sign of weakening demand for memory semiconductors, particularly high-bandwidth memory, or HBM. Still, uncertainty remains over Nvidia's longer-term product roadmap, given Huang's central role in shaping the company's business strategy and allocating resources. SK Hynix, another key supplier to Nvidia, reversed earlier gains to close 3.03% lower on Friday. In a research note earlier in the day, Shinhan Securities said investors had initially looked past concerns over Nvidia's leadership change and focused instead on the broader outlook for the AI industry. South Korea's Kospi also reversed earlier gains Friday. In a research note, iM Securities said the impact of Nvidia's leadership change on the broader semiconductor sector appeared limited, pointing to gains in AMD and Broadcom shares in the previous U.S. session and continued investment demand for AI companies. ASUS Co-CEO S.Y. Hsu told CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia " that Nvidia's leadership change was unlikely to alter its competitive advantages in the near term, though the company would monitor any impact on product quality, service costs and deliveries. "I think Nvidia's product and the total AI ecosystem, the advantage will not change overnight," Hsu said. ASUS, which works with Nvidia across graphics cards and AI servers, has yet to interact with interim CEO Colette Kress, Hsu said, adding that the company was seeking a meeting to better understand any potential strategic changes. Over the longer term, Hsu said Huang had played a key role in helping Nvidia and its partners accelerate innovation, and that he would be watching to see whether the company could maintain that pace without him.

Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation His fame extended way beyond tech. In May, Huang joined President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to China to meet with President Xi Jinping . Three months later, Huang gathered six of the biggest names at the Nasdaq to announce on CNBC a proposed $500 billion artificial intelligence buildout plan, cementing his central role at the intersection of Wall Street and Silicon Valley. As Nvidia became the first company to rip past a $5 trillion market cap, bending the laws of physics with its advanced graphics processing units and pushing the AI boom to seemingly endless bounds, the now 63-year-old Huang, clad in a black leather jacket, traversed the globe as the face of the brand powering the next industrial revolution. Over the past week it all came crashing down. Following two reported extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with an employee — Huang is leaving the company he co-founded 33 years ago in crisis, and thrusting the AI market into chaos. The board is now left to pick a successor for a company that's been run by a singular figure with no second-in-command. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Harvey Jones has been appointed chairman. Nvidia has not responded to multiple requests for comment. "How companies handle a crisis determines their future," former Cisco CEO John Chambers, now a startup investor, told CNBC's " Fast Money " on Wednesday. "How they handle this will determine if they're a great company and a great leadership team beyond one person." It had been a tumultuous stretch for Nvidia, even before the Huang saga led the board to launch an investigation of the CEO's behavior and the potential national security implications. The stock is on pace for its sixth straight weekly drop, which would be the longest losing streak since 2012. That includes a 9% slump last week after the midterm elections resulted in sweeping Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress, and the passage of dozens of ballot measures that could slow the buildout of new data centers. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday, and expectations remain high, with analysts projecting 92% year-over-year revenue growth to $109.2 billion, according to LSEG. That's up 18-fold from the same quarter in 2022, just before OpenAI launched ChatGPT and kicked off the generative AI era. It's a historic level of growth for any business, and particularly notable for a company that spent most of its first few decades as a niche technology provider for video games. Huang founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, he and other executives saw an opportunity to put GPUs to work for computationally intense projects. That technology eventually turned Nvidia into the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense. In the process, Huang became the ultimate decider, choosing how, when and where GPUs get allocated. The biggest buyers were the hyperscalers — Amazon, Google , Meta and Microsoft — which needed the chips to build their own AI services and make them available to cloud customers. OpenAI , meanwhile, was snapping up GPUs for its powerful models and consumer apps. To expand his customer base, Huang designated compute capacity to a number of so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius , putting equity into the companies and helping them build big businesses around renting out GPUs. Oracle gobbled up billions of dollars worth of GPUs, going heavily into debt in the process. Elon Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX , did the same to build its Grok model, before eventually starting to rent out excess capacity to Anthropic and Google. Huang wanted the world standardizing on Nvidia. Last year he demanded that Oracle buy additional Nvidia networking hardware if it wanted allocation to its state-of-the-art Grace Blackwell chips, said two people familiar with the deal who asked not to be named because the negotiations were private. In August, Nvidia said it will provide up to $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio that could be the largest of its kind in the world. "He created the product that started the industry," said Chris Miglino, CEO of neocloud Axe Compute . sources.text: The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models. Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community. Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion . Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source , whatever happens next. Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology. Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development. Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab. Huang’s influence extended beyond Nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem. Earlier this year, Huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, IBM, and Palantir, urging the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China. The impetus for that letter was Washington’s debate over how the U.S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections. That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons. Without Huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes. Huang’s exit could also strengthen the arguments of those in Washington who are arguing for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies, particularly as the scandal surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and alleged spy, puts renewed scrutiny on his efforts to loosen chip export controls. Restrictions on open-weight models from China could kneecap competition for American companies, the most powerful of which have kept their models closed. Still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project Huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy. As some of Nvidia’s biggest customers, including Google and OpenAI, develop their own chips, Nvidia has an incentive to cultivate a much broader ecosystem of AI developers and customers. More players training, fine-tuning, and running models mean more GPUs sold, and less dependence on a handful of frontier labs. Huang may be gone, but Nvidia still needs an open AI ecosystem. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority. TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment.
